identity.research_question: Under fixed preprocessing, architecture, training settings, and subject-independent LOPO evaluation, does adding localized eye-region information to a full-face RGB gaze-estimation baseline improve mean angular error on MPIIFaceGaze?
identity.hypothesis: Adding the localized 36x60 eye-region patches as an additional model input reduces mean LOPO angular error relative to the full-face-only reference run at identical training duration.
identity.changed_variable: input representation: face-only (resnet50) -> face + localized eye-region patches, left and right (resnet50_face_eyes)
fixed_variables: dataset: MPIIFaceGaze raw-txt layout (37,667 validated samples, p00-p14)
training duration: 3 epochs per fold (current working reference E3)

input_representation.reference_arm: face only, (B, 3, 224, 224) ImageNet-normalized float32 (model resnet50, frozen E3 results already exist)

treatment_arm.fusion: shared-weight compact CNN eye encoder (32-d per eye) concatenated with 2048-d face features -> linear head -> (B, 3)

identity.estimated_runtime_note: estimate only; based on measured E3 GPU runtime (~10.2 h) plus a small shared eye-encoder overhead

epochs.source: E3 ratified as working reference duration

seed.mechanism: apply_seed(0) before model construction and at trainer construction

pretrained_initialization.note: face backbone identical to baseline; eye encoder initialized from seed
pretrained_initialization.project_chosen_part: torchvision weight version PROJECT-CHOSEN / NOT AUTHORITATIVE

checkpoint.policy: existing trainer save/load; final-only per fold
